notice: Ground truth for a synthetic case. The evidence describes a fictional specialty outdoor retailer. No real Walmart data is used and no access to any Walmart system is claimed.
authoring_limitation: Authored by the same person who wrote the corpus. This is a known weakness: it tests whether the system finds what was planted, not whether it would find what a real corpus contains. Recorded in docs/04-evaluation.md rather than hidden.
question: Which intervention should the team prioritise to reduce losses from returns abuse?
desired_outcome: Reduce financial losses caused by abuse of the returns policy, without degrading the returns experience for legitimate customers and without creating unacceptable customer, associate, privacy, or legal risk.

scoring_rules.recall_denominator: Only entries with must_detect true count toward recall. GT-M6 is must_detect false: it is a real gap, but finding it is credit rather than a requirement. Hazards GT-H2 and GT-H3 are likewise recorded rather than required.
scoring_rules.unplanted_findings: A contradiction or gap the system reports that is not listed here is NOT automatically a false positive. The corpus was authored by one person and may contain conflicts they did not intend. Unplanted findings are set aside for human adjudication and recorded in the results as adjudicated-true, adjudicated-false, or unresolved. Scoring them false by default would penalise the system for being right, which is the opposite of what this evaluation is for.
scoring_rules.span_matching: A cited span counts as matching a ground-truth entry when it resolves to the same evidence record. Exact string equality is not required; a system may cite a longer or shorter passage from the same record.
scoring_rules.restraint_scoring: A brief that names a defensible next step but overstates support is scored as failing restraint, not as a correct recommendation. Naming the right option is necessary but not sufficient.
scoring_rules.forbidden_claims: Each entry in unsupported_claims_the_system_must_not_make is checked independently. Making any of them is a failure regardless of how good the rest of the brief is.

expected_contradictions.topic: the annual cost of returns abuse

side_a.span: Returns abuse costs the business $4.2M a year.

expected_contradictions.why_it_matters: The objectives document states as fact a midpoint whose own source gives a range spanning a factor of nearly six. The FY27 goal to recover $2.5M is set against the midpoint; at the low end of the range the entire loss is smaller than the recovery target.
expected_contradictions.how_to_resolve: The two are the same number with the uncertainty removed. The finance memo is the origin; the objectives document dropped the range and the method. Quote the range, or commission an internal measurement that narrows it.

expected_contradictions.topic: what the rising return rate is evidence of

side_a.span: The rise in return rate is the clearest signal we have that returns abuse is increasing

side_b.span: forty apparel SKUs were measured against the published size chart. Fourteen differed by more than one size increment, and all fourteen are in the Tarnside line introduced in 2025-Q3.

expected_contradictions.why_it_matters: A documented, non-abusive cause of returns enters the assortment in 2025-Q3, the quarter of the largest single-quarter rise in the return rate. The return-rate series therefore cannot be read as a measure of abuse without first removing causes of this kind, and the corpus contains at least two of them.
expected_contradictions.how_to_resolve: Neither statement can be settled from the corpus. Decomposing the rise by category mix and by the affected supplier line, and measuring the abuse rate directly, would separate them. Until then the rise is evidence that returns increased, not that abuse increased.

side_a.span: When we required receipts in the four pilot stores last autumn the returns stopped almost overnight.

side_b.span: No returns data was collected during the trial window, and no comparison stores were selected.

expected_contradictions.why_it_matters: A district manager is recalling a result the trial did not produce. The same four stores were in a remodel programme that reduced footfall over the same period, so even a real drop in returns would be unattributable. Treating the recollection as evidence would justify reintroducing a policy that was rolled back after customer escalations.
expected_contradictions.how_to_resolve: Ask which figures were seen. None were recorded. The trial cannot support a claim in either direction and would have to be rerun with a comparison group.

expected_contradictions.topic: whether the data the vendor platform requires exists

side_a.span: Orlin requires a nightly feed of 24 months of unified customer purchase and return history, keyed to a single customer identifier across all channels.

side_b.span: Until the returns data mart is delivered, customer return history cannot be joined across store and online channels, and no per-customer view of returns exists in any system.

expected_contradictions.why_it_matters: The vendor option's stated precondition does not exist and is not funded until FY28. Online item-level detail only begins at 2026-Q1, six quarters short of the 24 months required, and nothing earlier can be reconstructed. Any evaluation of the platform that ignores this is costing an option that cannot be deployed.
expected_contradictions.how_to_resolve: Ask the vendor what the product does with an unlinked, six-month, single-channel history, in numbers. Until that is answered, the platform cannot be compared with anything.

expected_missing_evidence.question: What share of returns is actually abusive?
expected_missing_evidence.why_it_matters: This is the quantity the question is about, and no document in the corpus measures it. Nine files discuss returns abuse; none establishes that any given return was abusive. Every option's value depends on a number nobody has.
expected_missing_evidence.how_to_obtain: A physical inspection audit of a random sample of returned units, with a written definition of what counts as abuse applied by trained inspectors. Finance costed one at $60,000 for a single quarter across eight stores and the returns hub.

expected_missing_evidence.question: How much of the six-quarter rise in return rate is explained by the shift in category mix?
expected_missing_evidence.why_it_matters: Apparel returns at 21.3% and hardgoods at 6.2%, and apparel's share of units sold rose from 31.0% to 46.0% over the same six quarters. A composition shift of that size can move the blended rate substantially with no change in customer behaviour, but per-category rates exist for the current quarter only, so the decomposition cannot be done.
expected_missing_evidence.how_to_obtain: Recover or recompute category-level return rates for 2025-Q1 onwards from the transaction record, then hold mix constant and re-derive the trend.

expected_missing_evidence.question: How concentrated are returns across customers?
expected_missing_evidence.why_it_matters: The whole shape of the answer depends on it. If a small number of customers drive a large share of returns, a targeted intervention is worth building; if returns are diffuse, only a policy or product change can move anything. No per-customer distribution exists in any system.
expected_missing_evidence.how_to_obtain: A one-off join of store and online return records on customer identifier, or the returns data mart deferred to FY28.

anchor.span: no per-customer view of returns exists in any system

expected_missing_evidence.question: What would returns friction cost in lost legitimate sales?
expected_missing_evidence.why_it_matters: Every intervention on the table adds friction to a returns process that most customers appear to be using as intended. The corpus contains no estimate of the revenue or lifetime-value cost of that friction, so the downside of every option is unpriced while the upside is quoted to one decimal place.
expected_missing_evidence.how_to_obtain: A holdout test of the specific friction proposed, measuring subsequent purchase behaviour, not only return volumes.

anchor.span: The proposal was rejected on that basis without a cost-benefit review

expected_missing_evidence.question: What does the organisation count as returns abuse?
expected_missing_evidence.why_it_matters: No written definition exists, and the people in the corpus plainly mean different things: worn-and-returned merchandise, a customer returning fourteen items, and ordering two sizes intending to return one. The third is described by customers as ordinary shopping and by the size-chart audit as a product defect. Nothing can be measured, and no vendor can be evaluated, until the term is defined.
expected_missing_evidence.how_to_obtain: A written definition agreed between merchandising, returns operations, finance and legal, expressed as conditions an inspector or a query could apply.

evidence_hazards.hazard: proxy metric standing in for the thing that matters
evidence_hazards.span: Return rate is the programme's headline measure of returns abuse.
evidence_hazards.description: The only quantitative series in the corpus measures the return rate. The programme has designated it the measure of returns abuse, set a target against it, and reads its six-quarter rise as evidence that abuse is increasing. The return rate counts returns, most of which the rest of the corpus describes in legitimate terms: reason codes are dominated by fit and quality, an audit shows the size chart is wrong for a line introduced in the quarter the rise steepened, and interviewed customers describe ordering two sizes as ordinary behaviour. The field that would carry the actual quantity, confirmed_abuse_cases, was added to the dashboard and never populated.
evidence_hazards.why_it_matters: Every claim in the brief about the size, direction or growth of returns abuse will be drawn from a series that does not measure it. This is the substitution that tempts GT-U2, GT-U3 and GT-U8, and it is not flagged anywhere in the corpus: no document says the return rate is a proxy. A brief that cites the trend as evidence about abuse has been misled by what the metric is called, not by what it counts.

evidence_hazards.hazard: composition shift inside a blended rate
evidence_hazards.description: The 2026-Q2 blended rate of 14.8% is the mix-weighted average of apparel at 21.3%, footwear at 17.9% and hardgoods at 6.2%, and apparel's share of units sold rose fifteen points over the six quarters of the trend. Part of the rise is arithmetic. How much cannot be established, because per-category rates were not retained before 2026-Q2.
evidence_hazards.why_it_matters: The headline series moves when the assortment moves. A brief that reads the trend as behavioural, in either direction, is attributing to customers something that may belong to merchandising.

evidence_hazards.span: This memo is the only quantified statement of returns-abuse losses in circulation.
evidence_hazards.description: The $4.2M figure appears in the objectives document, in the Chief Merchant's remarks and in the vendor's payback calculation. Three independent-looking corroborations of the loss are three restatements of one memo, each with the range and the source removed. The vendor's return-on-investment case is computed against Alderwick's own unmeasured number.
evidence_hazards.why_it_matters: Repetition across documents is the usual signal that a figure is well established. Here it is the opposite: the more places the number appears, the further it has travelled from the caveats it was issued with.

recommendation_restraint.reason: Nothing in the corpus measures the quantity the question is about. The only quantitative series measures the return rate, which counts returns rather than abuse, and its rise coincides with a fifteen-point category mix shift and a documented size-chart defect. The single loss figure is an external benchmark transposed onto an internal refund total, spanning $1.1M to $6.3M. The remainder is two self-selected store anecdotes out of 118 stores, one vendor claim with no method, and reason codes the customer chooses and nobody verifies. The corpus is large and almost none of it is load-bearing. No intervention can be defended above low support, and any option that acts on a named cause is acting on an assumption.
defensible_next_steps: Agree and write down a definition of returns abuse that an inspector or a query could apply, before any option is compared.
Commission the $60,000 physical inspection audit of a random sample of returned units to produce a first defensible abuse rate with an interval around it.
Decompose the six-quarter return-rate rise by category mix and by the Tarnside line before attributing any part of it to customer behaviour.
Add a verified disposition field at return receipt so the abuse rate becomes measurable in the normal course of operations.
Run a one-off cross-channel join of return history for a single district to establish whether returns are concentrated across customers at all.
If anything is trialled now, scope it to one district against matched control stores with the measure pre-registered; the 2025 four-store receipt trial produced no usable data.

must_not_recommend_without_conditions.why: The vendor's effect claim has no definition, baseline, client or method; the 24 months of unified cross-channel history it requires does not exist and is not funded until FY28; there are no confirmed cases to evaluate it against; $180,000 a year exceeds the CFO approval threshold; and no data protection assessment has been started.

Any automated score that refuses or restricts a return requires documented human review and a stated appeal path, and customer-level risk indicators may not be shown to store associates. Neither the cross-channel data nor the review capacity exists.
Returns-policy tightening is barred by the FY27 brand commitment and the loyalty terms, and the cost of added friction in lost legitimate sales is unmeasured everywhere in the corpus.

restraint_signals_that_must_appear: The brief must state that the rate of returns abuse is unmeasured, and that return rate is a count of returns rather than a measure of abuse.
The brief must not present the $4.2M figure as a measured loss, and should surface that its source gives a range of $1.1M to $6.3M.
The brief must state that two self-selected store observations out of 118 stores cannot establish a chain-wide pattern.
The brief must acknowledge that the corpus cannot rule returns abuse out either: the absence of measurement is not evidence that the problem is small.
The brief must recommend measurement, research or a scoped and controlled pilot rather than a full intervention, and must say what would have to be true for an intervention to become defensible.
